title: Stars trails over Armazones
caption: Star trails over Cerro Armazones, site of the Extremely Large Telescope, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at the ELT site, Cerro Armazones, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Dotted star trails curve across the sky above the top of Cerro Armazones, with a white and red tower at the centre of the picture. The image was assembled from multiple exposures taken on the 3046-metre-high summit, the site selected for ESO's Extremely Large Telescope.
As Earth rotates, the night sky seems to revolve around the southern celestial pole. Combine a series of exposures, and each star leaves a dotted trail showing how far it moved between shots.

The tower in the middle is the site's meteorological station, and on the left stands the Differential Image Motion Monitor, known as DIMM. The DIMM measures atmospheric seeing, the blurring of starlight by turbulence in the air above. Before a giant telescope is built, astronomers need to know how steady the air is and how the weather behaves, and these instruments were part of that survey.

understand.summary: This is a stack of night-time photographs taken in visible light with a camera on Cerro Armazones. The exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points; the dotted trails appear only because many exposures were stacked together.

explore: Good seeing is one of the most important qualities a site can have, because even the largest mirror cannot deliver sharp images through restless, turbulent air. Measurements like these help judge a site.
alt: Dotted star trails in the night sky above a white and red tower at the centre and a small instrument on the left.
